title: geogen save v1
description: A saved game: what `geogen.rules.Machine.save` returns and what the Godot runtime writes (`--save`, API `state.save`). Semantics: docs/rules.md, 'Saving'. World and actor state are separate sections, each a flat {key: value}: a key names its owner, so nothing is nested. Only values that differ from their declared defaults are stored; a key that is absent has its default. Bindings are never saved. A single-player game writes every section to one file; a server can keep the actor sections apart.

package.description: The package that was loaded when it was saved (written by the runtime).

now.description: Seconds the rules program has run: what timers' `at` is measured on.

clock.description: The world clock the conditions read.

world.description: Shared state. '<thing id>#<name>' is instance state: a declared variable of one placed instance, or an interaction ('<thing id>#<interaction>' is the state it is in or heading to, '<thing id>#<interaction>_locked' its lock). 'world:<package>.<name>' is a world variable. 'once:<rule>' and 'watch:<rule>' are the latches of rules that aren't per actor. An export without stable IDs keys its interactions '<node name>/<interaction>'.

actors.description: Per actor ('player', or an NPC's stable ID) its 'actor:<package>.<name>' values and the latches of per-actor rules.

actor_info.description: What the program knows of each actor besides its state. Optional: actors a save doesn't describe stay as the host knows them.

room.description: The room it is in ('' for none): `actor.room`.

timers.description: What is still to happen, in firing order (`at`, then `seq`).

seq.description: The order it was scheduled in: ties go to the lower.

kind.description: rule: a rule's `after` ran out, its effects are due. arrive: an interaction reaches the state it is heading to. dwell: a state's own `after` ran out, it moves on to its `then`.

state.description: kind arrive, dwell: the state it arrives at or dwells in.

actor.description: The actor behind it ('' or null: nobody).
